# Lerian Midaz — Full Reference

> Source-available (Elastic License 2.0) core banking platform in a single Go 1.27 monorepo (v4 module path, single root go.mod — no go.work) on `github.com/LerianStudio/lib-commons/v7` v7.14.0 + `lib-observability/v4` v4.6.1. Three deploy units: a unified Ledger HTTP API (onboarding + transaction + CRM holders/instruments + fees, :3002), a Tracer real-time transaction-validation / fraud-prevention API (:4020), plus an Infra docker-compose backing stack. Uses PostgreSQL (primary/replica), MongoDB (metadata + CRM + fees), RabbitMQ (async transactions), and Valkey/Redis (caching). Supports multi-tenant isolation via the lib-commons v7 tenant-manager.

---

## 1. Product Overview

Midaz is a source-available core banking platform in a single Go monorepo: a double-entry
ledger plus real-time transaction validation/fraud prevention (Tracer), CRM (holders/instruments),
and a fee engine — all in one repository, building from one
root `go.mod`. It is no longer "just a ledger"; the consolidation folded the surrounding banking
capabilities into the same repo. Transactional messaging (PIX, cards, wires) and governance
integrations remain external/marketplace. It implements a financial hierarchy:

```
Organization → Ledger → Asset
                      → Portfolio → Account
                      → Segment → Account
                      → Account Type
             → Transaction → Operation → Balance
```

Key capabilities:
- **Double-entry accounting**: Every transaction produces balanced debit/credit operations
- **N:N transactions**: Multiple sources and destinations in a single transaction
- **Multiple creation modes**: JSON, Inflow, Outflow, Annotation
- **Transaction lifecycle**: Create → Commit/Cancel/Revert (pending transactions support)
- **Async processing**: RabbitMQ-based balance updates with bulk recorder (10x throughput)
- **Multi-asset**: Currency (ISO-4217), crypto, commodities, custom asset types
- **Multi-tenant**: Database-per-tenant isolation via the lib-commons v7 tenant-manager
- **Accounting routes**: Configurable operation routes and transaction routes for validation
- **Real-time validation / fraud prevention (Tracer)**: CEL rule engine, multi-scope spending limits, two-phase reservations, and a hash-chained audit log, configurable per-ledger
- **Fees (embedded)**: fee engine + billing packages embedded in the ledger binary; fees applied on transaction create
- **CRM (folded)**: holder/instrument management folded into the ledger binary (host ledger's `midaz` namespace, org-scoped on `/v2/organizations/{organization_id}/...`)

## 2. Architecture

### 2.1 Deploy Units

Three deploy units: two Go services + infra. **CRM and fees are not deploy units** — CRM is a
package tree (`components/ledger/internal/crm`) imported by the ledger binary, and fees are embedded in the
ledger binary. Both are served on the ledger port `:3002`.

| Deploy unit | Port | Description | Data Stores |
|-------------|------|-------------|-------------|
| **Ledger** | 3002 | Unified HTTP API: onboarding + transaction + **CRM** (holders/instruments) + **fees** (engine + billing) | PostgreSQL (onboarding DB + transaction DB), MongoDB (metadata + CRM + fees), Redis/Valkey, RabbitMQ |
| **Tracer** | 4020 | Real-time transaction validation / fraud-prevention API (CEL rule engine, hash-chained audit) | PostgreSQL (own migrations) |
| **Infra** | — | Docker Compose backing stack (single source) | PostgreSQL 17 (primary/replica), MongoDB, RabbitMQ 4.1, Valkey, Grafana/OTEL-LGTM |

### 2.2 Pattern: Hexagonal Architecture with CQRS

```
Handlers (HTTP) → Services (Command/Query) → Repositories (Postgres/Mongo/Redis/RabbitMQ)
       ↓                    ↓                           ↓
    Models (pkg/mmodel)  Models                      Models
```

Dependencies flow inward. Inner layers must not depend on outer layers. Interfaces defined where used.

### 2.3 Directory Structure

```
midaz/
├── components/
│   ├── ledger/              # DEPLOY UNIT :3002 — onboarding + transaction + CRM + fees
│   │   ├── cmd/app/         # main.go entry point
│   │   ├── internal/
│   │   │   ├── adapters/
│   │   │   │   ├── http/in/ # Fiber HTTP handlers + routes (incl. fee_package_routes.go, holder_routes.go, instrument_routes.go, holder/instrument handlers)
│   │   │   │   ├── http/out/# Outbound HTTP clients
│   │   │   │   ├── postgres/# PostgreSQL repositories (onboarding + transaction)
│   │   │   │   ├── mongodb/ # MongoDB metadata + fees repositories
│   │   │   │   ├── redis/   # Redis/Valkey cache repositories
│   │   │   │   └── rabbitmq/# RabbitMQ producer/consumer
│   │   │   ├── bootstrap/   # Config, DI, server lifecycle, workers, initCRM, fee wiring
│   │   │   └── services/
│   │   │       ├── command/ # Write operations (CQRS)
│   │   │       ├── query/   # Read operations (CQRS)
│   │   │       └── fees/    # Embedded fee + billing-package use cases
│   │   ├── pkg/
│   │   │   ├── fee/         # Embedded fee engine
│   │   │   └── feeshared/   # Embedded fee shared types/constants (plugin-fees)
│   │   ├── migrations/
│   │   │   ├── onboarding/  # SQL migrations for onboarding DB
│   │   │   └── transaction/ # SQL migrations for transaction DB
│   │   └── api/             # OpenAPI 3.1 spec (openapi.huma.yaml, Huma-generated)
│   ├── crm/                 # PACKAGE TREE (not a deploy unit) — imported by ledger
│   │   ├── adapters/
│   │   │   └── mongodb/     # holder/ + instrument/ repositories
│   │   └── services/        # CRM business logic
│   │   # HTTP handlers/routes live in ledger http/in/ (midaz namespace); spec folds into ledger api/
│   ├── tracer/              # DEPLOY UNIT :4020 — real-time validation / fraud-prevention API (CEL, audit log)
│   │   ├── cmd/app/
│   │   ├── internal/
│   │   └── migrations/      # Tracer's own SQL migrations
│   └── infra/               # DEPLOY UNIT — Docker Compose backing stack (single source)
│       ├── docker-compose.yml
│       ├── postgres/        # Init scripts
│       ├── mongo/           # Replica set init
│       ├── rabbitmq/        # Definitions, config
│       └── grafana/         # OTEL collector config
├── pkg/                     # Shared packages (root)
│   ├── mmodel/              # Domain models (incl. Holder, Instrument)
│   ├── constant/            # Error codes (ledger 0001+, gap at 0130; 30 CRM-00xx: CRM-0006..CRM-0043), action/module constants
│   ├── errors.go            # Typed error structs + ValidateBusinessError
│   ├── net/http/            # Middleware, pagination, protected routes
│   ├── mtransaction/        # Transaction processing utilities (renamed from the old transaction pkg)
│   ├── streaming/           # lib-streaming event modeling
│   ├── crypto/              # CRM crypto primitives: kms/vault/ (Vault Transit KEK), tink/ (DEKs), mode + resolver
│   ├── mongo/               # MongoDB utilities
│   ├── repository/          # Repository interfaces
│   ├── pagination/          # Pagination helpers
│   └── utils/               # General utilities
├── tests/                   # Shared test trees (root)
│   ├── chaos/, helpers/, utils/
├── scripts/                 # Build/CI scripts
├── mk/                      # Makefile includes (coverage, tests, quality)
├── docs/PROJECT_RULES.md    # Coding standards
├── docs/auth/RBAC-NAMESPACES.md  # The three authz namespaces (R9)
├── docs/api/SCOPING.md      # Path-based org scoping on every surface, no exceptions (R22 reversed)
├── Makefile                 # Root orchestrator
├── go.mod                   # Module: github.com/LerianStudio/midaz/v4 (single root go.mod)
└── go.sum
```

## 3. Domain Models

All models live in `pkg/mmodel/`. Key entities:

### 3.1 Organization
- Fields: ID, ParentOrganizationID, LegalName, DoingBusinessAs, LegalDocument, Address, Status, Metadata, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt, DeletedAt
- Address follows ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 for country codes

### 3.2 Ledger
- Fields: ID, Name, OrganizationID, Status, Settings, Metadata, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt, DeletedAt
- Settings has two branches: `accounting` validation (validateAccountType, validateRoutes, requireHolder — the last gates CRM holder linkage) and `tracer` (per-ledger tracer/fraud-prevention toggles)

### 3.3 Account
- Fields: ID, Name, ParentAccountID, EntityID, HolderID, AssetCode, OrganizationID, LedgerID, PortfolioID, SegmentID, Status, Alias, Type, Blocked, Metadata, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt, DeletedAt
- HolderID is the CRM ownership link — the formal owner of the account (distinct from EntityID, which is not the ownership link); this field ties CRM holders to ledger accounts
- Alias format: `@<identifier>` (unique per ledger)
- Type: user-defined (e.g., "deposit", "expense", "revenue"); "external" is system-reserved
- Sub-accounts via ParentAccountID

### 3.4 Asset
- Fields: ID, Name, Type, Code, Status, OrganizationID, LedgerID, Metadata, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt, DeletedAt
- Types: currency, crypto, commodities, others
- Code: uppercase alphanumeric; currency codes follow ISO-4217

### 3.5 Transaction
- Persisted fields: ID, ParentTransactionID, Description, Status, Amount (single decimal), AssetCode, ChartOfAccountsGroupName, Source ([]string aliases), Destination ([]string aliases), LedgerID, OrganizationID, Route (deprecated), RouteID, Metadata, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt, DeletedAt
- Status lifecycle: ACTIVE → (revert) | PENDING → COMMIT/CANCEL
- Source/Destination are arrays of account aliases; per-operation amount/share/remaining distribution is expressed in the transaction INPUT (Send) shape, not the persisted record
- Block and unblock (`/v1` `.../transactions/{block,unblock}`, `/v2` `/v2/transactions/{block,unblock}`) are direct transfers whose primary operations are typed `BLOCK`/`UNBLOCK`. A block never touches overdraft on any leg: a debit beyond available is refused with `0018` even when the balance allows overdraft, and a credit into a balance with outstanding overdraft adds the whole amount to available without repaying it, so the blocked amount returns whole. An unblock settles outstanding overdraft first, like any credit (available 0, 100 blocked, 10 of overdraft: unblocking 100 leaves available 90), and records the repayment as an `OVERDRAFT` operation on the `overdraft` balance. Neither is ever reverted: the revert answers `0539`; a block is undone by an unblock and an unblock by a new block

### 3.6 Balance
- Fields: ID, OrganizationID, LedgerID, AccountID, Alias, Key, AssetCode, Available, OnHold, AccountType, Direction, OverdraftUsed, AllowSending, AllowReceiving, Version, Settings (*BalanceSettings), Metadata, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt, DeletedAt
- Key (max 100) identifies the balance within an account; Direction is the accounting direction; OverdraftUsed tracks consumed overdraft; Settings carries per-balance config (overdraft, etc.)
- Optimistic concurrency via Version field (lock version)
- Supports additional balances per account (e.g., multi-currency)
- Balance history queries via timestamp
- POST additional balance with `settings.allowOverdraft=true` provisions the system-managed `overdraft` companion balance (key=`overdraft`, direction=`debit`, scope=`internal`)

### 3.7 Operation Route / Transaction Route
- Operation routes define per-operation rules (source/destination/bidirectional)
- Transaction routes compose multiple operation routes for accounting validation
- Routes belong to the organization: lookups, updates and deletes resolve by `(organization, id)`, and a transaction route may link operation routes created under different ledgers of the organization. `ledgerId` is provenance only — the ledger the route was created under, omitted for a route created at organization level (`/v2/organizations/{organization_id}/{operation,transaction}-routes`, served on `/v2` only). The ledger paths (`/v1` and `/v2`) record the path ledger on create and reach every route of the organization on list, get, patch and delete. Both paths authorize with the same `("midaz","operation-routes"|"transaction-routes",verb)` tuples
- `accountingEntries` keys: `direct`, `hold`, `commit`, `cancel`, `revert` (transaction-route actions) plus the entry-only `overdraft`, `block`, `unblock` and `crossLedger`
- `crossLedger` marks the cross-ledger bridge route: debit rubric = arriving from another ledger, credit rubric = leaving to another ledger, both required; the operation route must be `bidirectional` (`0162` otherwise) and carry no other entry (`0256`); it needs no `direct` entry and never counts in an action's template. A transaction route links at most one (`0256` on transaction-route create/update, and on operation-route update when a linked transaction route already has one)
- Account rules: alias-based or account-type-based validation
- Optional operation routes: a transaction route link is required or optional (`operation_transaction_route.optional`, default `false`). A transaction may leave an optional route unused, which is what lets a fee route stay linked when the fee does not apply; a leg that uses one is still validated like any other (`0117`, direction, account rule, overdraft, `0151`). Required links are counted as before (`0116`). The flag is registered on `/v2` only — `operationRoutes` lists the required links and `optionalOperationRoutes` the optional ones, in the request and the response — and honored by `/v1` and `/v2` transactions alike. `/v1` route bodies refuse `optionalOperationRoutes` (`0053`) and `/v1` reads list every link in `operationRoutes`. A `/v2` PATCH applies each list as a JSON merge patch (absent or `null` keeps it, `[]` removes it) and validates the result as a create: a route in both lists `0541`, fewer than two links `0104`, no required source or destination `0153`/`0154`, an optional `crossLedger` route `0256` (also on an operation-route update that gives a crossLedger entry to a route linked as optional). `transaction_route.created`/`updated` events are schema `1.2.0`: `operationRouteIds` keeps every link and `optionalOperationRouteIds` names the optional subset

### 3.8 Account Type
- Custom account types per organization/ledger
- KeyValue identifier (alphanumeric + underscore + hyphen)

### 3.9 Holder (CRM)
- Fields: ID, ExternalID, Type (NATURAL_PERSON | LEGAL_PERSON), Name, Document, Addresses, Contact, NaturalPerson, LegalPerson, Status, Metadata, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt, DeletedAt
- Customer/entity ownership record; holders are linked to ledger accounts via Account.HolderID
- PII fields (Name, Document, contact details) are persisted via field-level encryption with searchable hashing (lib-commons crypto) — see CRM adapters

### 3.10 Instrument (CRM)
- Fields: ID, Document, Type, LedgerID, AccountID, HolderID, BankingDetails, RegulatoryFields, RelatedParties, Metadata, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt, DeletedAt
- An instrument associates a holder with a ledger account (HolderID + AccountID); carries banking details, regulatory fields, and related parties

## 4. API Reference

The HTTP layer is **Huma v2 (OAS 3.1) over Fiber v3**: Fiber remains the runtime router, auth
chain, and middleware stack, while Huma sits on top to generate the OpenAPI contract and validate
typed request/response structs. The API error envelope is chosen by ROUTE VERSION: `>= /v2`
serializes **RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`** — a `type`/`title`/`status`/`detail`/`instance`
document extended with `code` and `entityType` — while `/v1` keeps the midaz v3
`{entityType?, title, message, code, fields?}` body at `application/json` for clients already in
production. The `(code, status)` tuple per business error is identical on both. The native
OpenAPI 3.1 spec and Scalar docs UI are served differently per component. The ledger serves one spec
and docs UI at the root — `/openapi.{json,yaml}` and `/docs` — from a single contract that carries
both its `/v1` and `/v2` paths. The tracer serves its own spec and docs UI under `/v1` —
`/v1/openapi.{json,yaml}` and `/v1/docs`. Both the ledger and the tracer gate them on
`OPENAPI_DOCS_ENABLED`, off by default — opt in with `OPENAPI_DOCS_ENABLED=true`.

### 4.1 Ledger API (port 3002)

The ledger serves both the `/v1` and `/v2` path prefixes on the single root contract; there is
no single base path. The onboarding resources below sit under `/v1`. The fee resources are
ledger-scoped under `/v2` (see section 4.3), the CRM resources are under `/v2`, and the v2
transaction surface (for example `POST /v2/transactions/direct`) is exposed under `/v2`.

`POST /v2/transactions/batch` accepts an ordered wrapper of direct and hold
transactions and applies all monetary effects in one all-or-none accounting execution.
It has no path or query parameters; each item must name one organization and ledger through
its legs, while distinct direct items may use different enabled ledgers. A batch containing
hold items remains single-ledger. The success wrapper contains transactions in logical order.
Batch idempotency uses the smallest participating organization/ledger scope; changing
which ledger appears first does not create another claim for the same key.
See [the atomic batch contract](docs/api/atomic-transaction-batch.md).

`POST /v2/transactions/direct` also accepts mixed-ledger legs when every participant enables
`settings.crossLedger.enabled`. It decomposes the request into one balanced transaction per
ledger, executes all parts atomically, and returns their shared persisted `groupId` with an
ordered `transactions` array. See [the cross-ledger contract](docs/api/cross-ledger-transactions.md).

`POST /v2/transactions/hold` accepts the same mixed-ledger shape but creates only PENDING
origin transactions; destinations remain absent until commit. V2 commit approves every origin
and creates every destination in one engine execution, while v2 cancel releases the origins and
creates no destination. Both lifecycle responses are singular for ordinary transactions and a
`groupId` plus ordered `transactions` for cross-ledger groups. `/v1` rejects grouped lifecycle
operations with `0252`; a second terminal action returns `0254`.

Cross-ledger groups work on ledgers that enable `accounting.validateRoutes` when every part
belongs to one organization: the request's organization-wide `routeId` covers every part, the
bridge legs of validating parts take the transaction route's `crossLedger` operation route, each
validating part is checked leg by leg, and the client legs of all parts of a phase together must
use every required route of that phase's template and no route outside it (`0116`/`0117`/`0151`; optional routes may be left unused; legs naming a route count even in
non-validating parts). A group spanning organizations with a validating participant returns
`0251`. See the "Accounting routes" section of the cross-ledger contract.

`POST /v2/organizations/:organization_id/ledgers/:ledger_id/transactions/:transaction_id/revert`
reverses the complete cross-ledger group when the selected transaction has a `groupId`. It
validates every member, executes all reversals atomically in reverse part order, and returns
the new `groupId`, the original `revertedGroupId`, and one parent-linked transaction per part.
The equivalent `/v1` request rejects a group member with `0252`.
Concurrent v2 reverts through different group members share one idempotency claim;
duplicates return `0084` (HTTP 409) or replay the original reversal group. A
completed second revert returns `0087` (HTTP 409).

Each cross-ledger group operation publishes one `transaction_group.{posted,committed,canceled,reverted}`
event (ce-subject = group ID, payload lists every materialized part with ledger, `role`
`origin|destination`, and status) on top of the per-part `transaction.*` events, which carry
`groupId` and `groupRole`. A hold or a replayed request publishes no group event. The
coordinators emit D6 operations `create_cross_ledger_transaction`, `create_cross_ledger_hold`,
`commit_cross_ledger_group`, `cancel_cross_ledger_group`, and `revert_cross_ledger_group`;
`atomic_transaction_batches_total` and `atomic_transaction_batch_duration_ms` carry
`scope=single|cross_ledger`; `cross_ledger_group_ledgers` observes ledgers per applied group.
Once per recovery cycle the runner aligns PENDING `transaction_group` rows with their settled
members (never moving balances), deletes member-less intents older than a day, and reports
disagreeing members in `cross_ledger_group_reconcile_total{result="inconsistent"}`.

| PATCH | .../transaction-routes/:transaction_route_id | Update transaction route |
| DELETE | .../transaction-routes/:transaction_route_id | Delete transaction route |
| POST | /v2/organizations/:organization_id/operation-routes | Create operation route at organization level (no `ledgerId`) |
| GET | /v2/organizations/:organization_id/operation-routes | List every operation route of the organization |
| GET | /v2/organizations/:organization_id/operation-routes/:operation_route_id | Get operation route |
| PATCH | /v2/organizations/:organization_id/operation-routes/:operation_route_id | Update operation route |
| DELETE | /v2/organizations/:organization_id/operation-routes/:operation_route_id | Delete operation route |
| POST | /v2/organizations/:organization_id/transaction-routes | Create transaction route at organization level (no `ledgerId`) |
| GET | /v2/organizations/:organization_id/transaction-routes | List every transaction route of the organization |
| GET | /v2/organizations/:organization_id/transaction-routes/:transaction_route_id | Get transaction route |
| PATCH | /v2/organizations/:organization_id/transaction-routes/:transaction_route_id | Update transaction route |
| DELETE | /v2/organizations/:organization_id/transaction-routes/:transaction_route_id | Delete transaction route |

**PATCH metadata.** Every PATCH whose body carries `metadata` (organization, ledger, portfolio,
segment, account, account type, asset, transaction, operation, operation and transaction routes,
holder, instrument) applies it as an RFC 7396 merge patch: no `metadata` key or `{}` leaves the
stored metadata untouched, `{"k": null}` deletes `k`, any other key is added or replaced.
`"metadata": null` deletes every client key on `/v1` (the ledger's reserved fee keys stay) and
leaves the stored metadata untouched on `/v2`, which deletes keys one at a time. See
`docs/api/SCOPING.md`.

#### Settings / Metadata

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| POST | /v1/settings/metadata-indexes/entities/:entity_name | Create metadata index |
| GET | /v1/settings/metadata-indexes | List metadata indexes |
| DELETE | /v1/settings/metadata-indexes/entities/:entity_name/key/:index_key | Delete metadata index |

#### System

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| GET | /health | Health check |
| GET | /readyz | Readiness probe |
| GET | /version | Version info |
| GET | /openapi.json | OpenAPI 3.1 spec (JSON) — served when `OPENAPI_DOCS_ENABLED=true` |
| GET | /openapi.yaml | OpenAPI 3.1 spec (YAML) — served when `OPENAPI_DOCS_ENABLED=true` |
| GET | /docs | Scalar API docs UI — served when `OPENAPI_DOCS_ENABLED=true` |

### 4.2 CRM API (served by the ledger binary on port 3002)

CRM (holders, instruments, related parties) is folded into the ledger binary — it is **not** a
standalone service. The holder/instrument handlers and routes live in the ledger HTTP tree
(`components/ledger/internal/adapters/http/in/`) so the unified Huma OpenAPI spec discovers them; they are
served on `:3002` under the host ledger's `midaz` authz namespace (the resources `holders` and
`instruments`); the standalone CRM plugin namespace was collapsed into `midaz` at v4 (see
`docs/auth/RBAC-NAMESPACES.md`, X1). Uses MongoDB for persistence; holder/instrument PII is encrypted
at rest, alongside deterministic HMAC search tokens that enable equality lookups over ciphertext. The
encryption backend is selected by `KMS_VENDOR`: unset/`none` uses legacy lib-commons symmetric crypto;
`hashicorp-vault` switches to **envelope mode** — a Vault Transit KEK wrapping per-organization Tink
DEKs — which also mounts the provision/status/audit routes below. See section 6.2 and
`docs/architecture/crm-field-encryption.md`.

Scoping is **path-based**: CRM endpoints read the organization from the `:organization_id` path
segment, UUID-validated by the protected-route chain (`ParseUUIDPathParameters`). The former
`X-Organization-Id` header and the `X-Ledger-Id` header were removed; `ledger_id` survives only as
an instrument create-body field and an optional `GET .../instruments` list filter. See
`docs/api/SCOPING.md` (R22 reversed).

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| POST | /v2/organizations/{organization_id}/holders | Create a holder (authz `midaz`/`holders`) |
| GET | /v2/organizations/{organization_id}/holders | List holders (authz `midaz`/`holders`) |
| GET | /v2/organizations/{organization_id}/holders/{holder_id} | Get a holder (authz `midaz`/`holders`) |
| PATCH | /v2/organizations/{organization_id}/holders/{holder_id} | Update a holder (authz `midaz`/`holders`) |
| DELETE | /v2/organizations/{organization_id}/holders/{holder_id} | Delete a holder (authz `midaz`/`holders`) |
| GET | /v2/organizations/{organization_id}/holders/{holder_id}/accounts | List a holder's accounts org-wide across every ledger, with an optional `?ledger_id=` narrowing filter (authz `midaz`/`holders`; mounted only when the ledger account-query backing is non-nil) |
| GET | /v2/organizations/{organization_id}/instruments | List instruments (authz `midaz`/`instruments`) |
| POST | /v2/organizations/{organization_id}/holders/{holder_id}/instruments | Create an instrument for a holder (authz `midaz`/`instruments`) |
| GET | /v2/organizations/{organization_id}/holders/{holder_id}/instruments/{instrument_id} | Get an instrument (authz `midaz`/`instruments`) |
| PATCH | /v2/organizations/{organization_id}/holders/{holder_id}/instruments/{instrument_id} | Update an instrument (authz `midaz`/`instruments`) |
| DELETE | /v2/organizations/{organization_id}/holders/{holder_id}/instruments/{instrument_id} | Delete an instrument (authz `midaz`/`instruments`) |
| DELETE | /v2/organizations/{organization_id}/holders/{holder_id}/instruments/{instrument_id}/related-parties/{related_party_id} | Remove a related party from an instrument (authz `midaz`/`instruments`) |
| POST | /v2/organizations/{organization_id}/encryption/provision | Provision org encryption keys (authz `midaz`/`encryption`; envelope mode only) |
| GET | /v2/organizations/{organization_id}/encryption/status | Encryption provisioning status (authz `midaz`/`encryption`; envelope mode only) |
| GET | /v2/organizations/{organization_id}/protection/audit | PII protection audit (authz `midaz`/`protection`; envelope mode only) |
| POST | /v2/organizations/{organization_id}/ledgers/{ledger_id}/holders/:holder_id/accounts | Create a holder ↔ account association (composition; authz `midaz`/`accounts`; always mounted) |

The three encryption/protection routes are registered **only in envelope mode** (`KMS_VENDOR=hashicorp-vault`);
in legacy mode their handlers are nil and the routes are never mounted.

The holder-account composition (`POST`) carries an extra `:ledger_id` segment because it creates a
real ledger account; the holder-accounts `GET` (`HolderAccountsHandler.GetAccountsByHolder`, mounted
only when the ledger account-query backing is non-nil) lists a holder's accounts across every ledger
of the organization and needs no ledger. It accepts an optional `?ledger_id=` narrowing filter; a
malformed value is `0082` / 400. Because it reads the onboarding stores rather than the CRM ones, it
is the one CRM-path route carrying its own `holder-accounts` route options. The `POST` (`CompositionHandler.CreateHolderAccount`, in `composition_routes.go`) is
always mounted. Holder ownership is org-scoped (matching Mongo storage), not ledger-scoped.

CRM error responses carry **canonical midaz codes** (e.g. `0009`, `0046`, `0047`, `0094`) — the
legacy `CRM-00xx` transform shim was removed. The 30 CRM domain sentinels (section 5.1)
are still emitted on their own paths.

### 4.3 Fees API (served by the ledger binary on port 3002)

The fee engine + billing-package surface is embedded in the ledger binary — it is **not** a
standalone service. Routes are registered in
`components/ledger/internal/adapters/http/in/fee_package_routes.go` and its billing siblings (ledger-scoped, `/v2`), under the
`plugin-fees` authz namespace and served on `:3002`.

Scoping is **path-based**: fee endpoints read the organization and ledger from the
`:organization_id` and `:ledger_id` path segments, UUID-validated by the protected-route chain
(`ParseUUIDPathParameters`) — the same convention as every other surface in the binary. The former
`X-Organization-Id` header was removed; path-validation errors return the canonical midaz
`ErrInvalidPathParameter` envelope (fee business errors use the canonical numeric error-code
registry in `pkg/constant/errors.go` — the `FEE-` prefixed code family is retired). See
`docs/api/SCOPING.md`.

The fifteen operations are served under the ledger-scoped `/v2` contract (`{base}` =
`/v2/organizations/{organization_id}/ledgers/{ledger_id}`); the path names the ledger and a read
reaches only what that ledger owns.

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| POST | {base}/packages | Create fee package |
| GET | {base}/packages | List the ledger's fee packages |
| GET | {base}/packages/:package_id | Get fee package |
| PATCH | {base}/packages/:package_id | Update fee package |
| DELETE | {base}/packages/:package_id | Delete fee package |
| POST | {base}/estimates | Estimate fee calculation (dry run) |
| POST | {base}/billing-packages | Create billing package |
| GET | {base}/billing-packages | List the ledger's billing packages |
| GET | {base}/billing-packages/:billing_package_id | Get billing package |
| PATCH | {base}/billing-packages/:billing_package_id | Update billing package |
| DELETE | {base}/billing-packages/:billing_package_id | Delete billing package |
| POST | {base}/billing/calculate | Calculate billing |
| GET | {base}/fee-debts | List the ledger's fee debts, oldest first; `?status=open\|settled` filters, `?account_alias=` narrows to one debtor and adds `openTotal`, what it owes over all its open debts |
| GET | {base}/fee-debts/:fee_debt_id | Get fee debt |
| POST | {base}/fee-debts/collect | Collect a debtor's open fee debt now (see below) |

On the `/v2` paths the path is the sole authority on the ledger: the nil UUID is refused as a
`ledger_id` path value, `ledgerId` was removed from the create/estimate/calculate request bodies
(a body that still sends it is rejected as an unknown field, `400`; the former mismatch guard and
its `0234` code are retired), and `?ledgerId=` is refused on the two listings (`0235`) — its empty
value would mean "every ledger", the one scope a ledger-scoped listing must not express. Authz is
`plugin-fees` with the usual `(resource, verb)` tuples.

A package is scoped by up to three create-only selectors plus its amount band: `transactionRoute`,
`segmentId`, and `metadataSelector`, a flat map of key/value pairs the transaction's `metadata` must
all carry as equal strings (a numeric metadata value never matches). A package applies to a
transaction only when every selector it carries matches and the amount is inside its band; when
several apply, the one carrying the most selectors wins, each metadata pair counting one, and a tie
is refused (`0198`). Two packages on overlapping bands collide (`0184`/`0199`) only when their
selectors are identical.

A fee key inside a package's `fees` map must match `^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$` and is stored and returned
verbatim: create refuses any other key with `400` naming `fees.<key>`, and update applies the rule
only to a key that adds a fee, so a stored key of any shape stays editable and removable; an added
key equal to a stored key except for letter case is refused with `400`, and the stored key must be used,
unless the same update removes that stored key, which renames the fee (the new key must still match
the grammar).

A fee may set `deferrable` (optional, default `false`, returned on every read). When the payer
cannot fund a deferrable fee, the unfunded share opens a fee debt that the payer's later credits
settle, oldest first, instead of refusing the transaction with `0018`; the debt is listed on
`{base}/fee-debts`. Deferral acts only on `/v2` direct transactions; `/v1` creates and `/v2`
hold/commit still refuse with `0018`. Only a fee with `isDeductibleFrom: false` can be deferrable:
create or update leaving a fee both deductible and deferrable is refused with `0530` (422). The
transaction then records the send plus the fee, less the debt it opened (send 100, fee 10, payer
holds 105: amount 105, debt 5). Enable it only once every ledger pod
runs a release that knows fee debt (see `docs/architecture/engine.md`).

A package switched off (`enable: false`) or deleted may keep applying, and a fee whose
`deferrable` changed to `false` may still open fee debt when unfunded, for up to 60 seconds when a
transaction read the packages concurrently with the change.

Closing an account is permanent. To retire a fee account, point the fee package at the new fee
account and leave the old account open: reverts of earlier transactions and collections of fee
debt already owed to it still post there.

`POST {base}/fee-debts/collect` takes `{accountAlias, balanceKey?, maxAmount?}` and settles the
debtor balance's open fee debt from its available balance, oldest debt first, in one transaction
capped at `maxAmount` and at what the balance owes. It charges no fee and never originates a debt.
An optional `X-Idempotency` header makes a retry return the first collection; an answer that settled
nothing is not kept, and without the header every call is a new collection. A debtor balance that is blocked, cannot send, closing, closed, deleted,
debit-direction or external collects nothing; the collection stops at the first debt whose fee
account is blocked, cannot receive, closing, closed, deleted, debit-direction, external, in
overdraft or of another asset. It answers
`200 {collected, transactionId?}`; nothing settled is
`{"collected":"0"}` with no transaction. The transaction carries `metadata.feeDebtCollection =
"true"`, its amount is what it settled, and reverting it is refused (`0089`). Authz is
`midaz:fee-debts:post`.

Live fee calculation (`POST .../fees`) is intentionally **not** exposed — fees run in-process via
the transaction-create seam, not over HTTP.

### 4.4 Tracer API (port 4020)

Real-time transaction validation / fraud-prevention API. Hexagonal + CQRS, CEL rule engine,
hash-chained audit log. Ships its own SQL migrations under `components/tracer/migrations`. This is
an INDEPENDENT spec/port/deploy unit — it is not folded into `:3002`. Base path: `/v1`.

The ledger reaches Tracer over a separate reservation seam, not the `:4020` REST API. The seam is
the gRPC service `lerian.midaz.reservation.v1.ReservationService` (`proto/reservation/v1`), which the
tracer always serves on `TRACER_GRPC_PORT` (default `:4021`); it is the only surface that drives the
reservation lifecycle (reserve, confirm, release), and the ledger is its only caller. The ledger turns
the seam on by setting `TRACER_BASE_URL` to the seam address (an `http://`/`https://` scheme is
tolerated and stripped; empty injects a nil reserver, leaving the transaction-create path unchanged).
The ledger presents at most one credential on every seam call. With `PLUGIN_AUTH_ENABLED=true` it
is an Access Manager application token (gRPC metadata `authorization: Bearer <token>`) minted from a
credential dedicated to the tracer: `TRACER_M2M_CLIENT_ID`/`TRACER_M2M_CLIENT_SECRET` in
single-tenant mode (both required), and in multi-tenant mode the calling tenant's own credential read
at `tenants/{ENV_NAME}/{tenant UUID without dashes}/ledger/m2m/tracer/credentials` on the backend
`M2M_SECRETS_BACKEND` selects (`aws`, the default: AWS Secrets Manager; `vault`: HashiCorp Vault KV v2 under `M2M_VAULT_MOUNT`, connected through `VAULT_ADDR`/`VAULT_TOKEN`/`VAULT_CACERT`/`VAULT_NAMESPACE`); the static pair is never a fallback. Tokens are cached per credential and refreshed at 80% of their
lifetime, served until `exp` − 30s (90% of the lifetime for a token too short for that margin): the
still-valid token is served while one background mint runs (each failed one logs Warn), and each
token schedules its own refresh so an idle tenant normally finds a valid token. A failed or deferred
refresh is retried while the token is valid (backoff from 1s, doubling, capped at a quarter of the
refresh-to-expiry span, never inside the failure window, never past expiry), so only an outage outlasting that span lets it expire.
Past 30 idle minutes the token is no longer refreshed but stays served until it expires, and the
tenant is then forgotten. A
caller waits for a mint only when no valid token is cached, for at most `TRACER_M2M_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS`
(default 3000) and within its own deadline; `TRACER_TIMEOUT_MS` and `tracer.timeoutMs` bound only the
RPC sent once the token is in hand. One that gives up sent nothing and fails as plain unavailable, not counted. The multi-tenant token is minted on
the tenant's first call on each pod, an expected `failPosture` event when that mint outlasts `TRACER_M2M_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS`.
A failed mint opens a per-tenant failure window every caller and scheduled refresh honours (1s,
doubling per consecutive failure, capped at 15s, plus up to 25% random jitter; reset by a successful
mint). A token whose `exp` is not after its mint is a failed mint; a lifetime is capped at 24h. A call the tracer answers `Unauthenticated` invalidates only the
rejected token and is retried once with a fresh one, unless that token is younger than 5s (then the
rejection is returned, so a rejecting tracer costs at most one mint per tenant per 5s). A tenant
credential stays cached until the Access Manager refuses it or mints an empty token (transient mint
failures keep it); because lib-auth reports a 5xx or 429 as a refusal too, a refusal drops it at most
once per tenant per 30s; a missing secret is cached 5s, a malformed one 30s, a transient read failure never. A credential the
ledger cannot obtain is never sent: the call fails as unavailable (`failPosture`, `0178` when
closed), logged once at Error and counted in
`tracer_reservation_credential_rejected_total{operation,reason="not_sent"}`. Without plugin auth the credential is `TRACER_API_KEY` as `x-api-key` (never retried);
with neither, nothing is sent. Plugin auth plus `TRACER_API_KEY` refuses boot. The tracer enforces
the first identity its configuration enables — token (`PLUGIN_AUTH_ENABLED=true`), API key
(`API_KEY_ENABLED=true`), transport (`TRACER_TLS_MODE=mtls|mesh`), none. Under the token every RPC is
authorized against the Access Manager as `tracer/reservations:post`; only application tokens pass,
their `azp` (client id) or `sub` must be in `TRACER_SEAM_ALLOWED_CLIENTS` in single-tenant mode, and in multi-tenant mode
their `name` claim must be `ledger-m2m-tracer-{tenant}` for the token's own `tenantId` claim (tenants
compared canonically),
`AUTH_M2M_INVERSION_ENABLED=true` is recommended (without it the tracer boots with a Warn and the
Access Manager authorizes application tokens under a shared editor role, so only the allowlist or the
ledger client name binding restricts who may reserve), `AUTH_CACHE_TTL` must be greater than zero under
`DEPLOYMENT_MODE=saas` (boot refusal; a boot Warn elsewhere), and the tenant is the token's `tenantId` claim
(`x-tenant-id`, still sent by the ledger, is only cross-checked; UUID and dashless forms compare
equal). Under every other identity, all single-tenant, `x-tenant-id` carries the tenant. A missing
or invalid token or API key answers `Unauthenticated`, an Access Manager or guard refusal
`PermissionDenied`, an unreachable Access Manager `Unavailable`. A seam with no identity boots with
one Warn in BYOC and `local` and refuses to boot under `DEPLOYMENT_MODE=saas` or in multi-tenant
mode; `DEPLOYMENT_MODE=saas` also refuses a token or API key on a plaintext seam. `TRACER_TLS_MODE`
selects the transport: `mtls` (both sides present certificates; the tracer's gRPC listener also
requires the client cert's DNS SAN or URI SAN, or CN on a cert without SANs, to match
`TRACER_TLS_CLIENT_ALLOWED_NAMES`), `server` (the tracer's gRPC listener presents its certificate,
the ledger verifies it against `TRACER_TLS_CA_FILE`, no client certificate), `mesh` (plaintext behind
a sidecar that must enforce STRICT mTLS), or empty (plaintext). In multi-tenant mode a tenant that is
not provisioned, suspended or purged answers `Unavailable` (`0534`). A reserve replayed onto a transaction whose reservation already settled (released,
expired or confirmed) answers `FailedPrecondition` (`0533`), which an `enforce` ledger turns into
`0532`. A confirm reports how many rows it confirmed and how many it found already released
(`already_released`); the ledger does not fail the commit on such rows but logs a Warn, adds a span
event and increments `tracer_reservation_confirm_already_released_total{operation}`, because that
spend is never counted. See
[docs/architecture/ledger-tracer-topology.md](docs/architecture/ledger-tracer-topology.md).

A `/v2` reserve carries the fee-inclusive amount and asset (any Midaz asset code: 1 to 100
uppercase Unicode letters, the ledger's own grammar), the transaction date (only a future date is
refused; its age is not bounded), the first internal source account's `accountId` and ledger account
`type`, the transaction metadata filtered to the tracer's key rules (`^[a-zA-Z0-9_]+$`, at most 64
characters, at most 50 entries, values as strings — so reserve-path CEL rules must compare strings),
and `revert=true` for a `/v2` revert. The tracer evaluates its CEL rules before its limits and answers
`decision` (`ALLOW`/`DENY`/`REVIEW`) beside `denied`. On reserve only a matched rule refuses (the
tracer's `DEFAULT_DECISION_WHEN_NO_MATCH` is ignored), a rule that cannot be evaluated refuses as
`REVIEW` with `reason=rule_evaluation_error`, and a revert skips the rules but still reserves its
limits. Under `tracer.mode=enforce` a limit `DENY` rejects with `0177`, a rule `DENY` with `0535`, a
`REVIEW` with `0531`, a refused request with `0532`, a rejected seam credential (gRPC
`Unauthenticated`/`PermissionDenied`) with `0536` when `failPosture` is closed (it proceeds when open
and is logged at Error and counted in
`tracer_reservation_credential_rejected_total{operation,reason="rejected"}` in every mode),
and an unavailable tracer (including a tenant whose rule cache is not loaded yet or
that reached the tracer's per-tenant worker cap: gRPC `Unavailable`/`0445`)
branches on `failPosture` (`0178` when closed); `advisory` never blocks, and a transaction it lets
through after a refusal holds no reservation, so its spend is never counted. A reserve that was
sent and then timed out or was cancelled before the tracer answered may still have reserved
capacity, so the ledger settles it by transaction, best-effort and without changing the response:
it confirms when the movement applied and the transaction is not PENDING, and releases on a `0178`
rejection or an engine abort. A tracer that answered with an error (including `Unavailable`) or a
call that was never sent held nothing and is not settled. The settle never runs on the request
path: a dedicated queue (64 in flight, a full queue drops with a warning) waits `3s` (the tracer's
reserve lock wait) plus `TRACER_TIMEOUT_MS` before each of at most two attempts, the second only
when the first failed or settled nothing, and then logs a warning with the transaction id. An atomic batch or
a cross-ledger v2 commit whose execution hand-off fails releases the reservations held for its items.
Evaluation continues past a rule that cannot be evaluated: a matched `DENY` still decides, otherwise
the answer is `REVIEW`; the tracer's `POST /v1/validations` answers the same way, with HTTP 200
`decision=REVIEW`, `reason=rule_evaluation_error`. `tracer.timeoutMs`
(default `250`, applied to every ledger that never stored it) bounds each reserve call, with
`TRACER_TIMEOUT_MS` only as the ceiling. Deploy the tracer before the ledger and do not roll the tracer
back below this contract. See [docs/api/SCOPING.md](docs/api/SCOPING.md).

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| POST | /v1/rules | Create rule |
| GET | /v1/rules | List rules |
| GET | /v1/rules/:rule_id | Get rule |
| PATCH | /v1/rules/:rule_id | Update rule |
| DELETE | /v1/rules/:rule_id | Delete rule |
| POST | /v1/rules/:rule_id/draft | Move rule to draft |
| POST | /v1/rules/:rule_id/activate | Activate rule |
| POST | /v1/rules/:rule_id/deactivate | Deactivate rule |
| POST | /v1/limits | Create limit |
| GET | /v1/limits | List limits |
| GET | /v1/limits/:limit_id | Get limit |
| PATCH | /v1/limits/:limit_id | Update limit |
| DELETE | /v1/limits/:limit_id | Delete limit |
| POST | /v1/limits/:limit_id/draft | Move limit to draft |
| POST | /v1/limits/:limit_id/activate | Activate limit |
| POST | /v1/limits/:limit_id/deactivate | Deactivate limit |
| GET | /v1/limits/:limit_id/usage | Get limit usage |
| POST | /v1/validations | Run validation |
| GET | /v1/validations | List validations |
| GET | /v1/validations/:validation_id | Get validation |
| GET | /v1/audit-events | List audit events |
| GET | /v1/audit-events/:audit_event_id | Get audit event |
| GET | /v1/audit-events/:audit_event_id/verify | Verify the audit-event hash chain |

The two-phase reservation flow (a reservation holds projected limit usage, then is confirmed on
commit or released on rollback, by reservation ID or by the originating transaction ID) is served
only by the gRPC seam above; the HTTP API has no reservation route. Every confirm and release that settles a row
writes a `RESERVATION_CONFIRMED`/`RESERVATION_RELEASED` audit event that `GET /v1/audit-events` returns.

#### System

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| GET | /health | Health check |
| GET | /readyz | Readiness probe |
| GET | /metrics | Prometheus metrics |
| GET | /version | Version info |
| GET | /v1/openapi.{json,yaml} | OpenAPI 3.1 spec — served when `OPENAPI_DOCS_ENABLED=true` |
| GET | /v1/docs | Scalar API docs UI — served when `OPENAPI_DOCS_ENABLED=true` |

## 5. Error System

### 5.1 Error Codes (pkg/constant/errors.go)

Numeric ledger codes starting at 0001 (non-contiguous; gap at 0130). 30 CRM domain codes prefixed
with `CRM-` (CRM-0006..CRM-0043, non-contiguous). The registry is numeric-only for the core; the
`FEE-` / `TRC-` / `TPL-` / `REP-` prefixed families are retired (0 survivors). API errors are emitted
in the envelope the route version serves (§4) — RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` on `>= /v2`, the
midaz v3 body on `/v1` — preserving each sentinel's `(code, status)` tuple on both.

#### Ledger Error Codes (selected key codes)
- `0007` ErrEntityNotFound — entity not found
- `0009` ErrMissingFieldsInRequest — required fields missing
- `0018` ErrInsufficientFunds — insufficient funds; also a block debit beyond available, even with overdraft allowed
- `0020` ErrAliasUnavailability — alias already in use
- `0041` ErrTokenMissing — no auth token
- `0042` ErrInvalidToken — expired/invalid token
- `0043` ErrInsufficientPrivileges — forbidden
- `0046` ErrInternalServer — unexpected server error
- `0047` ErrBadRequest — malformed request
- `0084` ErrIdempotencyKey — duplicate idempotency key
- `0086` ErrLockVersionAccountBalance — race condition detected
- `0095` ErrMessageBrokerUnavailable — RabbitMQ down
- `0097` ErrOverFlowInt64 — integer overflow
- `0125` ErrInvalidTransactionNonPositiveValue — zero/negative value
- `0146` ErrTenantNotProvisioned — tenant DB not initialized
- `0159` ErrTenantServiceSuspended — tenant service suspended
- `0160` ErrTenantNotFound — tenant does not exist
- `0161` ErrTenantServiceUnavailable — tenant resolution failed
- `0514` ErrTransactionBatchCardinality — batch item count is outside the configured 1–50 bound (HTTP 400)
- `0515` ErrTransactionBatchInputLegsLimitExceeded — aggregate debit/credit legs exceed 1,000 (HTTP 400)
- `0516` ErrTransactionBatchBudgetExceeded — derived post-fee work or serialized state exceeds a fixed batch budget (HTTP 422)
- `0517` ErrTransactionBatchStructuralValidation — one or more batch items fail structural validation (HTTP 400)
- `0539` ErrBlockUnblockNotRevertible — a revert targets a block or an unblock; undo a block with an unblock and an unblock with a new block (HTTP 422)

#### Overdraft Feature Error Codes (0167–0175, 0492)
- `0167` ErrOverdraftLimitExceeded — transaction exceeds overdraft limit
- `0168` ErrDirectOperationOnInternalBalance — user operation targets internal-scope balance
- `0169` ErrDeletionOfInternalBalance — delete targets internal-scope balance
- `0170` ErrReservedBalanceKey — client used system-managed balance key (e.g. "overdraft")
- `0171` ErrInvalidBalanceDirection — unsupported direction enum value
- `0172` ErrInvalidBalanceSettings — settings payload fails validation
- `0173` ErrOverdraftLimitBelowUsage — cannot reduce limit below current usage
- `0174` ErrStaleBalanceVersion — balance modified between read and write (retry needed)
- `0175` ErrUpdateOfInternalBalance — PATCH targets internal-scope balance
- `0492` ErrOverdraftRouteNotConfigured — overdraft leg's route lacks a direction-specific overdraft accounting entry (route validation enabled)

#### Settings / Reservation Error Codes (0176–0178, 0531–0536, 0249–0256)
- `0176` ErrInvalidSettingsFieldValue — settings field value fails validation: `tracer.mode` outside `off|advisory|enforce`, `tracer.failPosture` outside `open|closed`, or `tracer.timeoutMs` outside the closed range `1..30000` ms. Raised at the shared write-time validation, so `POST .../ledgers` and `PATCH .../ledgers/{ledger_id}/settings` reject identically
- `0177` ErrTransactionReservationDenied — tracer reservation denied by a limit (`reason=limit_exceeded`) under `tracer.mode=enforce` (HTTP 422)
- `0178` ErrTransactionReservationUnavailable — tracer unreachable or failing under `tracer.mode=enforce` + `tracer.failPosture=closed` (HTTP 503)
- `0531` ErrTransactionReservationReview — a tracer rule flagged the transaction for `REVIEW`, or a rule could not be evaluated for it (`reason=rule_evaluation_error`), under `tracer.mode=enforce`; rejected before the balance commit (HTTP 422)
- `0532` ErrTransactionReservationRejected — the tracer refused the reserve request itself (gRPC `InvalidArgument`/`FailedPrecondition`) under `tracer.mode=enforce`, whatever the `failPosture` (HTTP 422)
- `0533` ErrReservationAlreadySettled — tracer seam: a reserve replayed onto a transaction whose reservation is already released, expired or confirmed; gRPC `FailedPrecondition`, surfaced by an `enforce` ledger as `0532`
- `0534` ErrReservationTenantInactive — tracer seam: the call's tenant is not provisioned or not active; gRPC `Unavailable`, which the ledger routes through `failPosture`
- `0535` ErrTransactionReservationRuleDenied — a tracer rule answered `DENY` under `tracer.mode=enforce`; rejected before the balance commit, the rule's reason is not returned (HTTP 422)
- `0536` ErrTransactionReservationUnauthorized — the tracer reservation seam rejected the ledger's credential (gRPC `Unauthenticated`/`PermissionDenied`: missing or invalid token, wrong API key, client not granted or not allowlisted) under `tracer.mode=enforce` + `tracer.failPosture=closed`; check the ledger's Access Manager client and the tracer's allowed clients (HTTP 503)
- `0249` ErrCrossLedgerNotEnabled — at least one ledger did not opt in through `crossLedger.enabled`; the policy resolver returns HTTP 422 and identifies the disabled ledger
- `0250` ErrCrossLedgerAssetMismatch — a direct cross-ledger request contains incompatible assets (HTTP 422)
- `0251` ErrCrossLedgerRouteValidationUnsupported — the cross-ledger group spans more than one organization and at least one participant validates accounting routes; routes belong to one organization (HTTP 422)
- `0252` ErrCrossLedgerLifecycleRequiresV2 — `/v1` attempted to commit, cancel, or revert a member of a cross-ledger group (HTTP 422)
- `0253` ErrCrossLedgerGroupIncomplete — the requested cross-ledger group is missing or has inconsistent intent or members (HTTP 422)
- `0254` ErrCrossLedgerGroupNotPending — grouped commit/cancel targeted a group whose current status is not PENDING (HTTP 422)
- `0255` ErrCrossLedgerRouteNotConfigured — a participant validates routes but the request's transaction route links no operation route with a `crossLedger` entry for the bridge leg (HTTP 422)
- `0256` ErrInvalidCrossLedgerRoute — the bridge route does not resolve to exactly one operation route: a `crossLedger` entry combined with other entries, more than one `crossLedger` operation route in a transaction route, or a `crossLedger` route linked as optional (HTTP 422)
- `0541` ErrOperationRouteBothRequiredAndOptional — a transaction route create or `/v2` update would list the same operation route in `operationRoutes` and `optionalOperationRoutes` (HTTP 400)

#### CRM Error Codes (all 30)
- `CRM-0006` ErrHolderNotFound — holder not found
- `CRM-0008` ErrInstrumentNotFound — instrument not found
- `CRM-0010` ErrDocumentAssociationError — document association error
- `CRM-0013` ErrAccountAlreadyAssociated — account already associated
- `CRM-0017` ErrHolderHasInstruments — holder has instruments (cannot delete)
- `CRM-0019` ErrMetadataQueryInvalidFormat — metadata query format error
- `CRM-0020` ErrMetadataQueryInvalidKey — metadata query invalid key
- `CRM-0021` ErrMetadataQueryContainsOperator — metadata query contains operator
- `CRM-0022` ErrInvalidHeaderValue — invalid header value
- `CRM-0023` ErrInstrumentClosingDateBeforeCreation — closing date before creation
- `CRM-0024` ErrRelatedPartyNotFound — related party not found
- `CRM-0025` ErrInvalidRelatedPartyRole — invalid related party role
- `CRM-0026` ErrRelatedPartyDocumentRequired — document required
- `CRM-0027` ErrRelatedPartyNameRequired — name required
- `CRM-0028` ErrRelatedPartyStartDateRequired — start date required
- `CRM-0029` ErrRelatedPartyEndDateInvalid — end date before start date
- `CRM-0030` ErrHolderHasAccounts — holder has accounts (cannot delete)
- `CRM-0042` ErrInvalidInstrumentAccountType — invalid instrument regulatory account type
- `CRM-0043` ErrBankAccountAlreadyRegistered — bank account (bankId and account, same branch, leading zeros ignored when both are numeric, or one of them without a branch) already registered to another live instrument of the organization (409)

Field-encryption / KMS family (envelope mode; see §6.2 and `docs/architecture/crm-field-encryption.md`):
- `CRM-0031` ErrKeysetNotFound — org encryption keyset not found
- `CRM-0032` ErrKeysetAlreadyExists — org encryption keyset already exists
- `CRM-0033` ErrKeysetRevisionConflict — keyset optimistic-concurrency conflict
- `CRM-0034` ErrRegistryNotFound — protection registry record not found
- `CRM-0035` ErrRegistryAlreadyExists — protection registry record already exists
- `CRM-0036` ErrRegistryRevisionConflict — registry optimistic-concurrency conflict
- `CRM-0037` ErrOrganizationEncryptionFailed — org field encrypt/decrypt failed
- `CRM-0038` ErrProvisioningFailed — key provisioning failed
- `CRM-0039` ErrAuditEventRequired — protection audit event required
- `CRM-0040` ErrAuditWriteFailed — protection audit write failed
- `CRM-0041` ErrReservedTenantID — reserved tenant id (`default`) may not be provisioned externally

### 5.2 Error Types (pkg/errors.go)

| Type | HTTP Status | Use Case |
|------|-------------|----------|
| EntityNotFoundError | 404 | Entity not found |
| ValidationError | 400 | Input validation failures |
| EntityConflictError | 409 | Duplicate entities |
| UnauthorizedError | 401 | Missing/invalid auth |
| ForbiddenError | 403 | Insufficient privileges |
| UnprocessableOperationError | 422 | Business rule violations |
| FailedPreconditionError | 500 | Configuration errors. Despite the name, this maps to 500, not 412: a failed precondition here is a server misconfiguration, not a client-supplied condition |
| ServiceUnavailableError | 503 | Infrastructure failures |
| InternalServerError | 500 | Unexpected errors |
| ValidationKnownFieldsError | 400 | Field-level validation |
| ValidationUnknownFieldsError | 400 | Unexpected fields |

### 5.3 Error Handling Pattern

```go
// Business errors: return directly
if errors.Is(err, constant.ErrEntityNotFound) {
    return nil, pkg.ValidateBusinessError(constant.ErrEntityNotFound, "Entity")
}

// Technical errors: wrap with context
return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create entity: %w", err)
```

## 6. Environment Variables

Source of truth: `components/ledger/internal/bootstrap/config.go` (the unified Ledger Config
struct — also holds the CRM and fees Mongo config since both are folded into the ledger binary),
plus `components/tracer/.env.example` for the tracer deploy unit. Defaults in parentheses
are set programmatically by `applyConfigDefaults()`.

**There is no version env var.** The release links the identity into each binary (`-X main.version/revision/buildTime`, fed by the CI build args `VERSION`, `REVISION` and `BUILD_TIME`), and that single source feeds `GET /version`, the `version`/`revision`/`buildTime` fields of `/readyz`, the OTel `service.version` and `vcs.ref.head.revision`, the streaming manifest `appVersion` and the overdraft event version. `docker run <image> --version` prints the identity plus the dependency manifest; `GET /version` returns the identity alone. A build without those args reports `dev`/`unknown`.

#### Streaming (lib-streaming/v4 v4.1.0 / Kafka)
The master flag is `STREAMING_ENABLED`; when false, a no-op emitter is injected. The rest are
loaded by `libStreaming.LoadConfig()` with franz-go defaults. Wire format: CloudEvents 1.0 binary
mode on Kafka.

One topic per producing application: every event a binary emits rides
`lerian.streaming.<app>`, with `<app>` being its `STREAMING_CLOUDEVENTS_SOURCE`: `ledger` (whose
one topic carries ledger core, fees and CRM alike) and `tracer`. A failed publish is copied to
`lerian.streaming.<app>.dlq`. Those two topics are an application's entire write surface, with
no exception. The source is accepted only when it is exactly the application's roster
name (`ledger` for the ledger binary, `tracer` for tracer); any other non-blank value, malformed
or merely different, is rejected at startup, never normalized, and the check runs even when
`STREAMING_ENABLED=false`. A blank value (unset or whitespace-only) defaults to the roster name
before that check, so omission passes it; an enabled producer must still set the variable, since
`libStreaming.LoadConfig()` fail-closes on a missing source. `ce-type` is
`studio.lerian.<app>.<resourceType>.<eventType>`; schema version travels only in
`ce-schemaversion`, and tenant only in `ce-tenantid`.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| STREAMING_ENABLED | false | Enable streaming producer |
| STREAMING_BROKERS | — | Kafka-compatible broker list |
| STREAMING_CLIENT_ID | — | Producer client ID |
| STREAMING_CLOUDEVENTS_SOURCE | — | CloudEvents source (set explicitly per component) |
| STREAMING_COMPRESSION | — | Producer compression codec |
| STREAMING_REQUIRED_ACKS | — | Producer required acks |
| STREAMING_BATCH_LINGER_MS | — | Producer batch linger (ms) |
| STREAMING_SASL_MECHANISM | — | SASL mechanism |
| STREAMING_SASL_USERNAME | — | SASL username |
| STREAMING_SASL_PASSWORD | — | SASL password |
| STREAMING_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT_SASL | — | Allow SASL over plaintext |
| STREAMING_IMPORTANT_EMIT_TIMEOUT_MS | 5000 | Bound on best-effort broker-publication latency |

#### Service Discovery (opt-in; no-op when SD_ENABLED=false)
Consul-backed registration + host resolution. Read by `libsd.ConfigFromEnv()`.
Disabled by default: a no-op Manager is wired and `Resolve` returns the static
fallback host. When `SD_ENABLED=true`, `SD_ADVERTISE_ADDRESS` is required —
enabling discovery with an empty advertise address aborts boot
(`ErrEmptyAdvertiseAddr`).

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| SD_ENABLED | false | Enable Consul-backed discovery (no-op when false) |
| SD_ADDRESS | localhost:8500 | Consul HTTPS API (host:port); :8501 on central agents |
| SD_ADVERTISE_ADDRESS | — | Required when enabled; hostname or full URL. Empty + enabled aborts boot |
| SD_ADVERTISE_PORT | 0 | Advertised port override; 0 = use Register port (SERVER_ADDRESS) |
| SD_WORKLOAD | — | Workload scope for tag-based isolation per environment |
| SD_TLS | false | Enable HTTPS to the discovery server |
| SD_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY | false | Skip discovery-server cert verification (dev/self-signed) |
| SD_TOKEN | — | ACL token sent to the discovery server |

#### Tracer Client (ledger → tracer)
| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| TRACER_BASE_URL | — | Tracer reservation seam address, gRPC `host:port` (enables reservation calls; an `http://`/`https://` scheme is stripped) |
| TRACER_TIMEOUT_MS | — | Client ceiling (ms) on every tracer RPC; the per-ledger `tracer.timeoutMs` (default 250) bounds the reserve RPC beneath it; neither bounds the token wait |
| TRACER_TLS_MODE | — | Seam transport: `mtls` (mutual TLS), `server` (verify the tracer's certificate, present none) or `mesh`/empty (plaintext, sidecar mTLS) |
| TRACER_TLS_CERT_FILE | — | Ledger client cert presented under `mtls` |
| TRACER_TLS_KEY_FILE | — | Ledger client key under `mtls` |
| TRACER_TLS_CA_FILE | — | CA used to verify the tracer's server cert under `mtls` and `server` |
| TRACER_M2M_CLIENT_ID | — | Single-tenant Access Manager client id the ledger mints its seam token with (required with `PLUGIN_AUTH_ENABLED=true`; multi-tenant reads each tenant's credential from the `M2M_SECRETS_BACKEND` backend instead) |
| TRACER_M2M_CLIENT_SECRET | — | Secret of `TRACER_M2M_CLIENT_ID`; never logged |
| TRACER_M2M_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS | `3000` | How long (ms) a seam call waits for a token that is not cached yet, before its RPC timeout starts; `1..5000` (the mint timeout), else boot refuses; read only with `PLUGIN_AUTH_ENABLED=true` |
| M2M_SECRETS_BACKEND | `aws` | Multi-tenant custody backend of the seam credentials: `aws` (AWS Secrets Manager, `AWS_REGION` + default credential chain) or `vault` (Vault KV v2 via `VAULT_ADDR`, `VAULT_TOKEN`, `VAULT_CACERT`, `VAULT_NAMESPACE`); any other value refuses boot; no fallback between backends |
| M2M_VAULT_MOUNT | `secret` | Vault KV v2 mount of the seam credentials when `M2M_SECRETS_BACKEND=vault` |
| TRACER_API_KEY | — | Tracer `API_KEY` sent as `x-api-key` when `PLUGIN_AUTH_ENABLED=false`; refuses boot together with plugin auth |

Seam topology and TLS posture: [docs/architecture/ledger-tracer-topology.md](docs/architecture/ledger-tracer-topology.md).

### 6.2 CRM + Fees (folded into the ledger binary)

Since CRM and fees are served by the ledger binary, their config lives in the unified ledger
Config struct (`components/ledger/internal/bootstrap/config.go`) and `components/ledger/.env.example`.
They use **namespaced** Mongo env vars so they do not collide with the ledger's onboarding /
transaction Mongo. They MAY point at the same Mongo deployment (separate logical DBs).

CRM Mongo (`MONGO_CRM_*`, read by `initCRM` via the `CrmPrefixed*` config fields):

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| MONGO_CRM_URI | mongodb | Connection URI scheme |
| MONGO_CRM_HOST | midaz-mongodb | MongoDB host |
| MONGO_CRM_NAME | crm | Database name |
| MONGO_CRM_USER | midaz | Username |
| MONGO_CRM_PASSWORD | lerian | Password |
| MONGO_CRM_PORT | 5703 | Port |
| MONGO_CRM_PARAMETERS | — | Extra connection parameters |
| MONGO_CRM_MAX_POOL_SIZE | 1000 | Max pool size |
| MONGO_CRM_TLS_CA_CERT | — | TLS CA cert path |
| LCRYPTO_HASH_SECRET_KEY | — | Legacy CRM PII HMAC secret — live in legacy mode; imported for legacy reads in envelope mode |
| LCRYPTO_ENCRYPT_SECRET_KEY | — | Legacy CRM PII AES key — live in legacy mode; imported for legacy reads in envelope mode |

##### CRM Field Encryption (KMS / envelope)

`KMS_VENDOR` selects the encryption backend for holder/instrument PII: unset/`none` → **legacy**
(the `LCRYPTO_*` symmetric keys above, no Vault); `hashicorp-vault` → **envelope** (a shared,
mode-derived Vault Transit engine — `transit-mt`/`transit-st` — whose KEK wraps per-organization
Tink DEKs; tenant isolation lives in the key **name** `{tenant}_org-{id}`, not per-tenant mounts).
The `FieldEncryptor` seam (`components/ledger/internal/crm/services/encryption`) is non-nil in both
modes; the keyset/registry/audit repos, Vault client, and provision/status/audit routes wire up only
in envelope mode. Key rotation is scaffolded, not yet active. Full design:
`docs/architecture/crm-field-encryption.md`.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| KMS_VENDOR | none | Mode selector: unset/`none` → legacy; `hashicorp-vault` → envelope; anything else fails boot |
| KMS_VAULT_ADDR | — | Vault server address (envelope only) |
| KMS_VAULT_AUTH_METHOD | — | `approle` \| `token`; sole driver of Vault auth; fails closed if unset/invalid in envelope mode |
| KMS_VAULT_ROLE_ID | — | AppRole role ID (when `KMS_VAULT_AUTH_METHOD=approle`) |
| KMS_VAULT_SECRET_ID | — | AppRole secret ID (when `KMS_VAULT_AUTH_METHOD=approle`) |

`token` auth uses the hardcoded dev root token and is permitted only when `DEPLOYMENT_MODE=local`;
`MULTI_TENANT_ENABLED` selects `transit-mt` vs `transit-st` and the MT key-naming / reserved-tenant
rules. New dependencies for envelope mode: `hashicorp/vault/api`, `tink-crypto/tink-go/v2`.

Fees Mongo (`MONGO_FEES_*`):

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| MONGO_FEES_URI | mongodb | Connection URI scheme |
| MONGO_FEES_HOST | midaz-mongodb | MongoDB host |
| MONGO_FEES_NAME | fees | Database name |
| MONGO_FEES_USER | midaz | Username |
| MONGO_FEES_PASSWORD | lerian | Password |
| MONGO_FEES_PORT | 5703 | Port |
| MONGO_FEES_PARAMETERS | — | Extra connection parameters |
| MONGO_FEES_MAX_POOL_SIZE | 100 | Max pool size |
| MONGO_FEES_TLS_CA_CERT | — | TLS CA cert path |

Auth and multi-tenant env vars (`PLUGIN_AUTH_*`, `MULTI_TENANT_*`) are shared across the whole
ledger binary (one set governs onboarding, transaction, CRM, and fees) — see section 6.1.

### 6.3 Tracer (port 4020)

Source: `components/tracer/.env.example`. Key vars: `SERVER_PORT` (4020), `SERVER_ADDRESS`,
`DEPLOYMENT_MODE`, `ALLOW_INSECURE_TLS`, `API_KEY` / `API_KEY_ENABLED`, `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`,
`DB_HOST` / `DB_USER` / `DB_PASSWORD` / `DB_NAME` / `DB_PORT` / `DB_SSL_MODE` (its own PostgreSQL),
plus the standard OTEL exporter vars. The ledger→tracer reservation seam (separate from the `:4020`
REST API) is governed server-side by `TRACER_GRPC_PORT` (the gRPC seam's listen address, always on;
empty resolves to `:4021`, distinct from `SERVER_PORT`) and the `TRACER_TLS_*` settings —
`TRACER_TLS_CERT_FILE` / `TRACER_TLS_KEY_FILE` for the server identity, `TRACER_TLS_CLIENT_CA_FILE` to
verify the ledger's client cert under `TRACER_TLS_MODE=mtls`, and `TRACER_TLS_CLIENT_ALLOWED_NAMES`
(comma-separated DNS SAN / URI SAN identities, or CN on a cert without SANs, the gRPC listener
accepts; empty accepts any CA-signed cert with a boot Warn, and refuses boot under
`DEPLOYMENT_MODE=saas` when the transport is the seam identity). `TRACER_TLS_MODE=server` serves TLS
on the gRPC listener only, without client certificates. The seam's caller identity is selected by
`PLUGIN_AUTH_ENABLED` (Access Manager token; `AUTH_M2M_INVERSION_ENABLED=true` recommended, a boot Warn without it; in
single-tenant mode it requires `TRACER_SEAM_ALLOWED_CLIENTS` outside `DEPLOYMENT_MODE=local`), then
`API_KEY_ENABLED` (the same `API_KEY`, as gRPC metadata `x-api-key`), then the transport; recommended
lib-auth knobs are `AUTH_CACHE_TTL=60s` (a value greater than zero is required under token identity
with `DEPLOYMENT_MODE=saas` and Warned about elsewhere), `AUTH_BREAKER_ENABLED=true` and
`AUTH_JWT_VERIFY_CERT`. Enable token identity on the tracer only after the ledger's credential is
provisioned and the ledger that sends tokens is deployed; a tracer that demands tokens first answers
`Unauthenticated`, which the ledger turns into `0536` under `enforce` + `closed` and proceeds past
under `open` or `advisory`. With
no identity the seam, like the HTTP listener without auth, refuses to boot only under
`DEPLOYMENT_MODE=saas` (read raw; unset is not local) or `MULTI_TENANT_ENABLED=true`, and boots with
one Warn elsewhere; see
[docs/architecture/ledger-tracer-topology.md](docs/architecture/ledger-tracer-topology.md).

## 7. Build & Development

### 7.1 Prerequisites

- Go 1.27.0 (`go.mod` `go 1.27.0`; component Docker builders and CI use toolchain 1.27.2, `golang:1.27.2-alpine`)
- Docker (with `docker compose`)
- golangci-lint v2.13.2

### 7.2 Makefile Commands

```bash
# Setup
make set-env                  # Copy .env.example → .env for all components
make dev-setup                # Install tools + git hooks + env files
make setup-git-hooks          # Configure git hooks

# Build & Run
make build                    # Build the deploy-unit binaries
make up                       # Start all services (infra → ledger → tracer)
make down                     # Stop all services
make restart                  # Restart all services
make rebuild-up               # Rebuild and restart
make logs                     # Show logs

# Quality
make lint                     # Lint all components
make format                   # Format code
make tidy                     # go mod tidy
make sec                      # Security checks (gosec + govulncheck)

# Testing
make test                     # Run all tests
make test-unit                # Unit tests
make test-integration         # Integration tests (testcontainers)
make test-fuzz                # Fuzz tests
make test-bench               # Benchmarks
make test-chaos-system        # Chaos tests with Docker stack

# Coverage
make coverage-unit            # Unit test coverage
make coverage-integration     # Integration test coverage
make coverage                 # All coverage

# Migrations
make migrate-lint             # Lint migrations
make migrate-create COMPONENT=onboarding NAME=my_migration

# Docs
make generate-docs            # Generate OpenAPI 3.1 specs (ledger, tracer)
```

### 7.3 Docker Images

- **Ledger** (onboarding + transaction + CRM + fees): multi-stage Go build → distroless,
  exposed port 3002, runs as `nonroot:nonroot`.
- **Tracer**: multi-stage Go build → distroless, exposed port 4020.

There is no standalone CRM image — CRM ships inside the ledger image.

## 9. Multi-Tenancy

When `MULTI_TENANT_ENABLED=true`:

1. **Requires** `PLUGIN_AUTH_ENABLED=true` (JWT provides tenant ID)
2. Tenant-manager client resolves per-tenant database connections
3. TenantMiddleware injects tenant-scoped PG/Mongo connections into request context
4. Event-driven tenant discovery via Redis Pub/Sub
5. TenantCache provides process-local caching with configurable TTL
6. On tenant suspend/delete: all connections (PG, Mongo, RabbitMQ) are closed and cache invalidated
7. RabbitMQ consumers are started/stopped per tenant dynamically
8. Modules: `onboarding` and `transaction` with independent PG and Mongo managers; CRM
   (authz namespace `midaz`, `MONGO_CRM_*`) and fees (authz namespace `plugin-fees`,
   `MONGO_FEES_*`) add their own namespaced Mongo tenant clients within the ledger binary
   (resolution via the lib-commons v7 tenant-manager)

## 10. Per-Call Control Skips

Callers can opt out of individual processing controls on a single request, but only
under a two-key gate. A skip is honored **only when both** keys are set:

1. The request asks for it (a `skip` object on the create body), **AND**
2. The ledger opts into it via `settings.overrides.allow*Skip` (all default `false`).

If the request asks but the per-ledger override is not enabled, the request is rejected
with **HTTP 422** (`ErrSkipNotPermitted`, error code `0490` → `UnprocessableOperationError`).
The resolver is `pkg/skip.ResolveSkipFor(control, requested, allowed)`.

| Control | Surface | Request flag | Ledger opt-in | Audit column |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fees | `/v2` transaction create (direct/hold/block/unblock) | `skip.fees` | `overrides.allowFeeSkip` | `transaction.fees_skipped` |
| Tracer | `/v2` transaction create (direct/hold/block/unblock) | `skip.tracer` | `overrides.allowTracerSkip` | `transaction.tracer_skipped` |
| Holder | `/v2` account create | `skip.holder` | `overrides.allowHolderSkip` | `account.holder_check_skipped` |

The surface column is the route CONTRACT, not just the path: every seam the skips gate is
`/v2` only. The two transaction flags live on `CreateTransactionV2Input` and nowhere else,
so a `/v1` transaction body naming `skip` is an UNKNOWN field and is rejected with
**HTTP 400** by the decoder — never 422, and `fees_skipped` / `tracer_skipped` can never be
true on a row created through `/v1`. `skip.holder` differs: it is still a known field on the
`/v1` account body, where it is inert. See § Account Holder Seam and `docs/api/SCOPING.md`.

Honored skips are persisted to audit columns (domain fields
`mtransaction.Transaction.FeesSkipped` / `.TracerSkipped`, `mmodel.Account.HolderCheckSkipped`)
and surface on the `transaction.*` and `account.created` streaming payloads.

**Non-goals / invariants:**
- A **revert always re-runs the tracer**; the reverse transaction does NOT inherit the
  parent's tracer skip.
- **Idempotency replay returns the first outcome only for the same request**: a replayer
  whose body differs (a skip included) under the same key answers `0084` (HTTP 409) and posts nothing.
- An **honored skip adds zero downstream work** — it short-circuits before the control's
  package lookup; it never replaces the control with a more expensive code path.

## 10a. Holder Seam (`/v2` only)

Account creation resolves a holder through the seam in
`components/ledger/internal/services/command/create_account.go`
(`resolveAccountHolder`): it reads the two holder gate keys
(`accounting.requireHolder`, `overrides.allowHolderSkip`), resolves the per-call skip,
enforces the requireHolder validation, and materialises the account's `holder_id` —
defaulting a non-external account to the organization's deterministic self-holder.

The seam is a **`/v2` contract**. `command.RouteHolderPolicy` travels from the transport
shell into the use case (`HolderOffV1` / `HolderOnV2`, `account_holder_policy.go`), and
`HolderOffV1` is the FIRST gate — it short-circuits before the ledger settings read. A
`/v1` account create therefore:

- links **no** holder: the row persists `holder_id = NULL` and `holder_check_skipped = false`;
- cannot be rejected by the requireHolder gate (`ErrHolderRequired` / `ErrHolderNotFound`);
- cannot be rejected for an unpermitted `skip.holder` (`ErrSkipNotPermitted`);
- performs no holder settings read at all.

`holderId` and `skip.holder` in a `/v1` body are inert. The `/v1` responses withhold both
holder keys (`in.AccountV1`, published as the `Account` component), so the fields have no
readable effect on that contract; `/v2` answers with the holder-bearing `AccountV2`
component. `/v1` shipped before the seam existed, and a client integrated against it must
not acquire a holder link — or a new rejection class — from a version upgrade.

The holder-account composition route (`POST /v2/.../holders/{holder_id}/accounts`) passes
`HolderOnV2`: it exists to link a holder, and is served on `/v2` only.

### Organization self-holder

`CreateOrganization` takes the same `RouteHolderPolicy` and gates `provisionSelfHolder`
on it. `POST /v1/organizations` writes **no** CRM holder record; `POST /v2/organizations`
provisions the deterministic `LEGAL_PERSON` self-holder as before. The organization is
persisted either way — the gate suppresses the side effect, not the resource — and the
idempotent backfill runner is still the repair path. `mmodel.Organization` carries no
holder field, so no response projection is involved and the two contracts share one
schema component; only the create terminal differs
(`CreateOrganization` / `CreateOrganizationV2`).

### Outside the seam on both contracts

- **The asset-created external account.** `CreateAsset` builds the implicit external
  account as an `mmodel.Account` and hands it straight to `AccountRepo.Create`, bypassing
  `CreateAccount`, so it reaches no holder seam and persists `holder_id = NULL`. That is
  also what the seam resolves for an external account, so the two paths agree.
- **Account update.** Ownership is immutable: `mmodel.UpdateAccountInput` has no
  `holderId` (and an unknown body field is a `400`), and neither `holder_id` nor
  `holder_check_skipped` appears in the update statement's SET list or in the
  merge-patch nullable-field set.

## 11. Testing

### Test Types
- **Unit tests**: `*_test.go` files alongside source
- **Integration tests**: `*_integration_test.go` with testcontainers
- **Fuzz tests**: `*_fuzz_test.go` for property-based testing
- **Property tests**: `*_property_test.go` for invariant verification
- **Chaos tests**: `*_chaos_test.go` for resilience testing
- **Goroutine leak detection**: `goleak_test.go` in bootstrap

### Build Tags
- `integration`: testcontainers-based integration tests
- No tag: unit tests (default)
